name: Awang Jernih
role: Orang Laut boatman called for royal rowing
bio: Jernih has promised a cousin a crossing. A summons from the Bintan governor, in Mahmud’s name, may take him away before he can make good on it.
notes: fact: Pires describes people brought by the Bintan governor to row when the king required it, for food rather than pay (Pires II, p. 264; port-labour.md §1)
inference: Thomaz identifies the Celates with Orang Laut and reads the obligation as naval service, not paid commercial lighterage (Thomaz pp. 76–77; port-labour.md §1)
gameplay: Jernih, his cousin and the missed crossing are invented; no general cargo-labor role is implied (port-labour.md §4)
